The direct four-line root reader and recursive all-TOC/XML walker have different enforced ownership/load contracts, not two copies of one parse operation.

items.what: The bracket-depth test (symbol token in "([{" => +1, in ")]}" => -1) is written three times: closing (phrases.py:112-123), arguments (:126-141) and declared (:144-172; jscpd 7-line clone of arguments).
items.why: The loops do different jobs (find the match, split on commas, pick top-level fields), so this is close to a small idiom; a shared `bracket_step(token) -> int` would remove the repeated predicate, and a change in what counts as a bracket (kind check, new token) would need three edits. closing uses a slightly different spelling of the same test.
items.reason: closing matches the end of one bracketed expression, arguments splits commas only at nesting depth zero, and declared recognizes declaration field lists. Their shared four-line depth increment/decrement is a parser idiom, while termination/output/token policies differ. There is no duplicated whole parse operation to consolidate safely.
